# `move` / `vmove` — reverse-engineering report (jot/jt v0.1.2)

## Global conventions (apply to every case below)

- **Application-level errors** (anything the app "handles") are printed to **stdout**, never stderr, always formatted as `\x1b[0;31merror\x1b[0m: <message>\n` (red `error`, then plain message, trailing newline), and the **exit code is still 0**.
- **Success messages** go to stdout; item/vault names are wrapped in blue: `\x1b[0;34m<name>\x1b[0m`. Exit code 0.
- **Argument-parsing (clap) errors** go to **stderr**, plain text, **exit code 2**, stdout empty.
- **Panics** (corrupted/missing state) go to stderr, **exit code 101**.
- Neither command **ever reads stdin** — conflicts are hard errors; piping `y`, `n`, or garbage changes nothing. The `conflict = true/false` config key has **no effect** on move/vmove.
- Neither command ever modifies the `history` field (stayed `history = []` in every probe) nor the `folder` field of any vault's `.jot/data`.
- State files: registry `$XDG_DATA_HOME/jot/vaults`, config `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/jot/config`, per-vault `<location>/<name>/.jot/data`. Registry maps `name -> location` where location is the **parent** dir; the vault dir on disk is `<location>/<name>`.

## Help text (verbatim)

`jt move -h` / `--help` (stdout, exit 0; `vmove -h` analogous with its own USAGE line):
```
executable-move 
move an item

USAGE:
    executable move <item type> <name> <new location>

ARGS:
    <item type>       move a vault (or vl) | note (or nt) | folder (or fd)
    <name>            name of item to be moved
    <new location>    path to new location of item (current folder as root in case of note or
                      folder)

OPTIONS:
    -h, --help    Print help information
```
```
executable-vmove 
move notes and folders to a different vault

USAGE:
    executable vmove <item type> <name> <vault name>

ARGS:
    <item type>     move a note (or nt) | folder (or fd)
    <name>          name of item to be moved
    <vault name>    name of vault to move the item to

OPTIONS:
    -h, --help    Print help information
```
(Note: program name is argv[0]-derived — `executable` here.)

## Aliases

- `mv` ≡ `move`, `vm` ≡ `vmove` (verified working).
- Item-type aliases: `vl`≡vault, `nt`≡note, `fd`≡folder, all verified.
- Item types are case-sensitive: `move NOTE x y` → exit 2, stderr `error: "NOTE" isn\'t a valid value for \'<item type>\'\n\t[possible values: vault, vl, note, nt, folder, fd]\n\nFor more information try --help\n`.

## Argument-count errors (clap, stderr, exit 2, stdout empty)

- `jt move` → `error: The following required arguments were not provided:\n    <item type>\n    <name>\n    <new location>\n\nUSAGE:\n    executable move <item type> <name> <new location>\n\nFor more information try --help\n`
- `jt move note` → same shape listing `<name>\n    <new location>`; `jt move note n` → lists only `<new location>`.
- `jt move note n d extra` → `error: Found argument 'extra' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context\n\nUSAGE:\n    executable move <item type> <name> <new location>\n\nFor more information try --help\n`
- `jt vmove` → lists `<item type>\n    <name>\n    <vault name>` with `USAGE:\n    executable vmove <item type> <name> <vault name>`; 2-arg and 4-arg variants analogous.
- `jt vmove vault a b` → exit 2, stderr `error: "vault" isn\'t a valid value for \'<item type>\'\n\t[possible values: note, nt, folder, fd]\n\nFor more information try --help\n` (same for `vl`; vmove rejects vault/vl at clap level, before any state is touched).
- `jt move foo x y` → exit 2, `error: "foo" isn\'t a valid value for \'<item type>\'\n\t[possible values: vault, vl, note, nt, folder, fd]\n\nFor more information try --help\n`.

## `move note|nt <name> <new location>`

Source is always `current_folder/<name>.md`; destination is a **folder** path resolved relative to current folder (or as an absolute real-FS path, see below).

Success: `note \x1b[0;34mnote2\x1b[0m moved\n`, file relocated, exit 0.

Path forms for `<new location>` (probed):
- `dirB`, `dirB/`, `./dirB`, `dirB//`, `dirB/../dest1` (stays in vault) → all work.
- `..` → parent folder; works, including up to vault root. From vault root, `..` → `error: path crosses the bounds of vault\n`.
- Absolute real-FS paths **inside** the vault work (e.g. `/tmp/probe-4/v1loc/alpha/dirA`).
- `/` (or any absolute path outside vault, e.g. `/etc`) → `error: path crosses the bounds of vault\n`.
- Leading-slash vault-relative paths from the README like `/dirA/` or `/dirB/` do **NOT** work — treated as real FS absolute paths: `/dirA/` → `error: couldn't find the path specified\n` (because `/dirA` doesn't exist on the real FS). There is **no vault-root-relative syntax**; root is reached via `..` chains.
- Nonexistent relative dest → `error: couldn't find the path specified\n`.
- Dest exists but is a file → `error: io error\n`.

Name handling:
- Plain names only; a name containing `/` (e.g. `dirB/note3`, `a/b`) → `error: invalid name\n` — but only *after* destination checks pass (see ordering).
- `note3.md` as name: conflict check treats it as the literal filename (a dest containing `note3.md` conflicts, reported as `a note named note3.md already exists...`); the extension is effectively normalized (Rust `with_extension("md")` semantics).
- `.` as name → conflict check does not fire (see below), then `error: no such file or directory (os error 2)\n`. `..` as name → `error: a note named .. already exists in this location\n` (dest/.. always exists).

Conflict: if `<dest>/<name>.md` exists → `error: a note named <name> already exists in this location\n` (stdout, exit 0, nothing moved, no prompt). A **directory** named `<name>` in dest does not conflict (falls through to os error 2 since `<name>.md` source doesn't exist / or succeeds if source exists — conflict is purely on the note file).

Check ordering (empirically established): resolve dest (must exist → else `couldn't find the path specified`) → bounds (`path crosses the bounds of vault`) → dest ≠ current folder (`new location is same as old location` — compares dest against the **current folder**, regardless of where the named item actually lives) → conflict (`a note named X already exists in this location`) → name validity (`invalid name`) → actual rename (missing source → `no such file or directory (os error 2)`).

Not inside a vault → `error: not inside a vault\n` (stdout, exit 0; config+registry auto-created as side effect).

## `move folder|fd <name> <new location>`

Same rules/messages as notes, with `folder` in messages: success `folder \x1b[0;34mdirB\x1b[0m moved\n`; conflict `error: a folder named dirB already exists in this location\n`. Folder conflict = `<dest>/<name>` exists (any type), so names `.` and `..` always conflict.

- Moves the whole directory tree recursively (contents preserved).
- **Moving a folder into its own descendant is a data-loss bug**: `move folder dirA dirA/dirB` prints `folder \x1b[0;34mdirA\x1b[0m moved\n`, exit 0, but the folder **and all its contents are deleted** from disk (nothing is moved anywhere).
- Moving the folder you're currently in: impossible by name (source lookup is `current_folder/<name>`; `dirA` isn't inside itself → os error 2). `move folder . ..` → `error: a folder named . already exists in this location\n`. When the current-folder's parent moves it from outside (cwd elsewhere), the vault's `.jot/data` `folder` field is **not** updated (goes stale; `list` etc. then misbehave/panic depending on path).
- Moving with mismatched item type (`move folder <a-note> ...` or `move note <a-folder> ...`) → `error: no such file or directory (os error 2)\n` (folder lookup has no `.md`, note lookup appends `.md`).

## `move vault|vl <name> <new location>`

- `<new location>` must be **absolute**: relative → `error: specified path isn't absolute\n`. Trailing slash OK.
- Success: `vault \x1b[0;34mbeta\x1b[0m moved\n`; the directory `<old>/<name>` is relocated to `<new>/<name>` on disk; registry updated (`name = '<new location>'`); the vault's own `.jot/data` `location` field updated; `name`/`folder`/`history` preserved. Works while inside the vault (including from a subfolder; session continues seamlessly).
- Nonexistent vault → `error: vault ghost doesn't exist\n`.
- Nonexistent dest dir → `error: no such file or directory (os error 2)\n`.
- Dest already containing a dir named `<name>` → `error: a folder named beta already exists in this location\n`.
- Dest == current location → `error: new location is same as old location\n`.
- Dest path is a file → `error: io error\n`.
- Check ordering: absoluteness → vault exists → dest exists → same-location → conflict.
- Multiple vaults may share one location; a vault may be moved **inside another vault's directory** (nesting works fine).
- Works without a current vault set (only registry needed).
- **Data-loss bug**: moving a vault into its own subdirectory (`move vault alpha /.../v4loc/alpha/dest1`) prints `error: couldn't find the path specified\n` (exit 0) but **deletes the entire vault directory**; registry entry left stale. Afterwards every command panics: stderr `\nthread 'main' (<pid>) panicked at src/state/vaults/vault.rs:44:28:\ncalled \`Option::unwrap()\` on a \`None\` value\nnote: run with \`RUST_BACKTRACE=1\` environment variable to display a backtrace\n`, exit 101.
- Moving a vault whose directory was deleted externally: prints `vault \x1b[0;34malpha\x1b[0m moved\n`, **recreates an empty vault dir** at the destination whose `.jot/data` contains only `folder = ''\nhistory = []\n` (no name/location → subsequent commands panic at vault.rs:44:28), and updates the registry.

Registry ordering observation: the registry is rewritten on each operation with the current/last-operated vault listed first (e.g. after `enter alpha`: `alpha` then `beta`; after creating beta with no current: `beta` then `alpha`).

## `vmove note|nt|folder|fd <name> <vault name>`

- Item must be in the **current folder** of the current vault (name lookup identical to `move`). Target is always the **root of the target vault** (no subfolder choice).
- Success: `note \x1b[0;34mnote3\x1b[0m moved to vault \x1b[0;34mbeta\x1b[0m\n` / `folder \x1b[0;34mdirB\x1b[0m moved to vault \x1b[0;34mbeta\x1b[0m\n`; file/tree actually moved; both vaults' `.jot/data` untouched (history/folder unchanged).
- `vault`/`vl` item type → clap rejection (see above), exit 2.
- Nonexistent target vault → `error: vault <NAME> doesn't exist\n` — **bug: it prints the item name, not the vault name** (e.g. `vmove note note4 gamma` → `error: vault note4 doesn't exist`; `vmove note ghost gamma` → `error: vault ghost doesn't exist`). This check runs before the source-exists check and before the current-vault check (fresh env with no vaults: `vmove note n v` → `error: vault n doesn't exist`).
- Nonexistent source item (target vault OK) → `error: no such file or directory (os error 2)\n`.
- Conflict in target vault root → same messages as `move`: `error: a note named note3 already exists in this location\n` / `error: a folder named dirB already exists in this location\n`; nothing moved.
- Same-vault vmove (`vmove note note4 alpha` while in alpha): stdout is the concatenation of an **uncolored, newline-less** notice and the error: `note note4 already exists in vault alpha\x1b[0;31merror\x1b[0m: new location is same as old location\n` (folder variant: `folder fd1 already exists in vault alpha\x1b[0;31merror\x1b[0m: new location is same as old location\n`). Nothing moved.
- Target vault whose directory was deleted externally → `error: no such file or directory (os error 2)\n`, nothing moved (no skeleton recreation, unlike `move vault`).

## Missing/corrupted state files

- Registry file missing entirely → auto-recreated as `[vaults]\n`; then `move note n d` → `error: not inside a vault\n`, `move vault v /tmp` → `error: vault v doesn't exist\n` (both stdout, exit 0).
- Registry TOML corrupted → **panic**, exit 101, stderr `\nthread 'main' (<pid>) panicked at src/traits.rs:24:21:\ncouldn't parse data\nnote: run with \`RUST_BACKTRACE=1\` environment variable to display a backtrace\n` (same for move and vmove, all item types).
- Current vault's `.jot/data` corrupted → same panic at `src/traits.rs:24:21`, even for `move vault` of an unrelated vault (current vault's data is always loaded).
- Current vault's `.jot/data` missing → the file is **recreated containing only** `folder = ''\nhistory = []\n`, then panic at `src/state/vaults/vault.rs:55:32` (`Option::unwrap()` on None), exit 101; panics persist on subsequent runs because `name`/`location` are absent.
- Config/registry are auto-created with defaults (`editor = 'nvim'`, `conflict = true`; `[vaults]`) on first use in a fresh environment.

All probing is complete. Here is the full byte-level specification.

# Probe report: `jot` (jt) v0.1.2 — commands `config`/`cf`, `open`/`op`, `opdir`/`od`

Binary: `/workspace/executable`. All runs with isolated `HOME=/tmp/probe-5`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/probe-5/.config`, `XDG_DATA_HOME=/tmp/probe-5/.data`. Exit codes, streams, and bytes verified per invocation. Note: panic messages contain the process PID in `thread 'main' (<pid>) panicked` — the PID varies per run.

## 0. Global behavior relevant to all three commands

**State file auto-creation.** On *any* real subcommand (even read-only ones like `config editor` or a bare `vault` list), before executing, the app creates missing state files:
- `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/jot/config` with exact content `editor = 'nvim'\nconflict = true\n`
- `$XDG_DATA_HOME/jot/vaults` with exact content `[vaults]\n`

`--help`, `-h`, `help`, bare invocation (no args), and unknown-command errors do **not** create any state files. If `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/`XDG_DATA_HOME` are unset, it falls back to `$HOME/.config/jot/config` and `$HOME/.local/share/jot/vaults`.

**Error conventions.**
- Application errors: printed to **stdout** (not stderr) as `\x1b[0;31merror\x1b[0m: <msg>\n`, **exit code 0**.
- CLI parse errors (clap): printed to **stderr**, **exit code 2**.
- Rust panics: printed to **stderr**, **exit code 101**.
- Top-level clap usage strings use the argv[0] basename `executable`; the `config` subcommand's usage instead hardcodes `jt config ...`.

**Aliases confirmed:** `cf` ≡ `config`, `op` ≡ `open`, `od` ≡ `opdir` (identical behavior, verified for read/set/open/opdir paths).

---

## 1. `config` / `cf`

### Help
`/workspace/executable config --help` (also `cf -h`): stdout, exit 0:
```
executable-config 
display, set or open config

USAGE:
    jt config <config type>
    jt config <config type> [config value]

ARGS:
    <config type>     name of config item to display or set
    <config value>    pass a value if config needs to be updated

OPTIONS:
    -h, --help    Print help information
```

### Read: `config <key>`
Only two valid keys: `editor`, `conflict` (case-sensitive).
- `config editor` → stdout `editor: \x1b[0;34mnvim\x1b[0m\n`, stderr empty, exit 0
- `config conflict` → stdout `conflict: \x1b[0;34mtrue\x1b[0m\n`, exit 0
- Value shown is the current value from the file (after `config editor ''`, `cf editor` prints `editor: \x1b[0;34m\x1b[0m\n`).

### Invalid key: `config foobar`
stderr, exit 2:
```
error: "foobar" isn't a valid value for '<config type>'
	[possible values: editor, conflict]

For more information try --help
```
Exact bytes: `b'error: "foobar" isn\'t a valid value for \'<config type>\'\n\t[possible values: editor, conflict]\n\nFor more information try --help\n'`. Empty string key behaves the same (`"" isn't a valid value...`). Case variants rejected (`EDITOR` same error); a close miss adds a suggestion, e.g. `config Editor` inserts `\n\tDid you mean "editor"?\n` before `\n\nFor more information try --help\n`.

### Extra args: `config editor extra args here`
stderr, exit 2: `b"error: Found argument 'args' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context\n\nUSAGE:\n    jt config <config type>\n    jt config <config type> [config value]\n\nFor more information try --help\n"`. Note only the *first* unexpected arg is named. Values starting with `-` are rejected as flags unless passed after `--` (`config -- editor` works): `config editor -x` → stderr exit 2 with the additional line `\n\tIf you tried to supply \`-x\` as a value rather than a flag, use \`-- -x\`\n`.

### Set: `config <key> <value>`
- `config editor vim` → stdout `set \x1b[0;34meditor\x1b[0m to \x1b[0;34mvim\x1b[0m\n`, exit 0. Config file rewritten entirely as:
  ```
  editor = 'vim'
  conflict = true
  ```
- Values with spaces kept verbatim: `config editor "code -w"` → file gets `editor = 'code -w'`.
- Value containing a single quote is serialized triple-quoted: `config editor "a'b"` → `editor = '''a'b'''`.
- Empty value allowed: `config editor ''` → `editor = ''`.
- **Setting rewrites the whole file through the TOML serializer**: any unknown extra keys present in the file (e.g. `bogus = 'x'`) are **dropped**; key order in output is `editor` then `conflict`.
- `config conflict false` → `set \x1b[0;34mconflict\x1b[0m to \x1b[0;34mfalse\x1b[0m\n`, file `conflict = false`.

### `config conflict <invalid bool>`
Value must be exactly `true` or `false` (Rust `bool::from_str`). `config conflict notbool`, `1`, `TRUE` → **panic**, exit 101, stdout empty, stderr:
```
\nthread 'main' (<pid>) panicked at src/state/config.rs:74:42:\ncalled `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: ParseBoolError\nnote: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace\n
```
Config file left unchanged.

### Bare `config` (open config in editor)
- Spawns the program named by the `editor` config value with **exactly one argument: the absolute path of the config file** (`/tmp/probe-5/.config/jot/config`). Verified via fake editor logging argv (`NARGS: 1`, `arg[0]=</tmp/probe-5/.config/jot/config>`); child cwd = jt's cwd.
- The editor string is used **literally as a program name** — no word splitting, no shell. `editor = 'code -w'` → tries to exec a file literally named `code -w` → fails "editor not found". PATH lookup works (`editor = 'fakeed'` found via PATH); absolute paths work.
- **Waits** for the editor to exit (2s-sleep editor: jt returned only after ~2s); child exit code **ignored** (editor `exit 7` → jt still exits 0); child inherits stdin/stdout/stderr (editor's `CHILD-STDOUT` appeared on jt's stdout, `CHILD-STDERR` on jt's stderr).
- On success: jt prints nothing, exit 0.
- Editor program not found: stdout `\x1b[0;31merror\x1b[0m: editor not found\n`, exit 0.
- Editor exists but not executable, or is a directory: stdout `\x1b[0;31merror\x1b[0m: undefined error: Permission denied (os error 13)\n`, exit 0.
- `EDITOR` env var is ignored (fresh env with `EDITOR=fakeed` still used default `nvim` → "editor not found").

### Config file state edge cases
- Deleted config file (or whole config dir, or both state dirs): recreated with defaults on next command; `config editor` then prints `nvim`. Vaults file also recreated (`[vaults]\n`) if missing.
- Corrupted TOML (`this is not = = toml [[[`), empty file, missing key (file with only `editor = 'emacs'`), or wrong types (`editor = 5`, `conflict = 'true'`): **panic**, exit 101, stdout empty, stderr `\nthread 'main' (<pid>) panicked at src/traits.rs:24:21:\ncouldn't parse data\nnote: run with \`RUST_BACKTRACE=1\` environment variable to display a backtrace\n`. File not modified.
- Unknown extra keys in the file are **tolerated on read** (serde ignores them); the file is preserved byte-for-byte until a `config set` rewrites it (dropping the extras).

---

## 2. `open` / `op`

### Help
`open --help` (also `op -h`): stdout, exit 0:
```
executable-open 
open a note (from the current folder)

USAGE:
    executable open <note name>

ARGS:
    <note name>    name of note to be opened

OPTIONS:
    -h, --help    Print help information
```

### Preconditions / arg errors
- No vault entered: stdout `\x1b[0;31merror\x1b[0m: not inside a vault\n`, exit 0. This check happens **before** name validation (`open a/b` outside a vault prints "not inside a vault", not "invalid name").
- Missing arg: stderr, exit 2: `b'error: The following required arguments were not provided:\n    <note name>\n\nUSAGE:\n    executable open <note name>\n\nFor more information try --help\n'`
- Extra arg (`open mynote extraarg`): stderr, exit 2: `b"error: Found argument 'extraarg' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context\n\nUSAGE:\n    executable open <note name>\n\nFor more information try --help\n"`. Dash-values need `--` (`open -- -x` → proceeds, prints "note -x not found").

### Name validation
Name containing `/` **or** `\` → stdout `\x1b[0;31merror\x1b[0m: invalid name\n`, exit 0. Verified: `a/b`, `sub/subnote`, `.jot/data`, `./`, `../vaultloc/v1/mynote`, `a\b`. Embedded newlines are *not* invalid (pass through to the not-found message).

### Name → path resolution (empirically determined)
Current folder path is built from the vault's own `.jot/data` fields: `<location>/<name>/<folder>` (the registry is only used to *locate* the data file at `<registry-location>/<vaultname>/.jot/data`; if the data file's `location` disagrees with the registry, the **data file wins** — verified: with data `location = '/tmp/WRONGLOC'`, open looked in `/tmp/WRONGLOC/v1`).

Observed rule (matches every probe): let `stem` = Rust `Path::new(name).file_stem()` semantics applied to the name:
- Normal names: target = `<folder>/<stem>.md` — i.e. **any existing extension is replaced** by `.md` (not appended). So `open mynote` and `open mynote.md` and `open mynote.MD` all open `<folder>/mynote.md`; `open a.b` opens `<folder>/a.md`; `open a.b.md` looks for `<folder>/a.b.md` (not found). Stem matching is case-sensitive (`MYNOTE`, `Mynote` → not found); extension case is irrelevant because it's replaced.
- Dotty names follow `file_stem`: `..x` → stem `.` → target `<folder>/..md`; `...` → stem `..` → `<folder>/...md`; `x..` → stem `x.` → `<folder>/x..md`; `.hidden` → `<folder>/.hidden.md`; `....` → `<folder>/....md`. All verified against real files I created (`open ..x` opened `..md`, `open ...` opened `...md`, `open x..` opened `x..md`).
- Special case: `open ..` (file_stem is `None`) uses the path **unchanged**: spawns the editor with `<current folder>/..` literally (e.g. `/tmp/probe-5/vaultloc/v1/..` at vault root, `/tmp/probe-5/vaultloc/v1/sub/..` in subfolder `sub`) — no `.md` appended, no canonicalization.
- Special case: `open .` **always** prints `note . not found` (verified even when the would-be target `<folder>/v1.md` existed).
- Existence check is a plain `Path::exists()`: a **directory** named `d.md` is happily "opened" by `open d` (editor spawned with `.../v1/d.md`).
- Success = spawn editor with the target as its single argv; failure = stdout `\x1b[0;31merror\x1b[0m: note <name> not found\n` (`<name>` verbatim, exit 0). Stray non-note files are never opened: `open stray.txt` → looks for `stray.md` → "note stray.txt not found"; `open exact` (file `exact` exists, no ext) → looks for `exact.md` → "note exact not found". Trailing spaces matter: `open "mynote "` → `note mynote  not found` (two spaces: one from name, one separator). Empty name: `note  not found`.

### Editor spawn semantics
Identical to bare `config`: literal program name (no splitting — `editor = 'fakeed -x'` → "editor not found"), single argv = target path, **waits** for exit (2s-sleep editor → jt blocked ~2.009s), exit code ignored (`exit 3` → jt 0), stdio inherited. On success jt prints nothing, exit 0. Missing editor → `\x1b[0;31merror\x1b[0m: editor not found\n`; non-executable editor → `\x1b[0;31merror\x1b[0m: undefined error: Permission denied (os error 13)\n`.

### State edge cases
- Corrupted `.jot/data`: panic exit 101, `src/traits.rs:24:21: couldn't parse data`.
- Vault dir missing on disk (`<registry-location>/<name>` gone): the command **recreates** `<location>/<name>/.jot/` and writes a skeleton data file containing only `folder = ''\nhistory = []\n` (no `name`/`location`), then panics exit 101: `src/state/vaults/vault.rs:44:28: called \`Option::unwrap()\` on a \`None\` value`.
- `folder` field pointing to a nonexistent directory: notes simply report "not found".
- Successful `open` causes **no** state-file changes (`history = []` unchanged).

---

## 3. `opdir` / `od`

### Help
`opdir --help` (also `od -h`): stdout, exit 0:
```
executable-opdir 
open current folder in file explorer

USAGE:
    executable opdir

OPTIONS:
    -h, --help    Print help information
```

### Behavior
- No vault entered: stdout `\x1b[0;31merror\x1b[0m: not inside a vault\n`, exit 0.
- Extra arg: stderr, exit 2: `b"error: Found argument 'extraarg' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context\n\nUSAGE:\n    executable opdir\n\nFor more information try --help\n"`.
- Spawns **`xdg-open`** — and only `xdg-open`. Stubs for `gio`, `gnome-open`, `kde-open`, `exo-open`, `gvfs-open`, `nautilus`, `dolphin`, `thunar`, `open` were each tried alone on PATH: none was ever invoked; without `xdg-open` the command fails. There is no fallback chain.
- Exactly **one argv**: the current folder as a plain string `<location>/<name>/<folder>` using the **data file's** fields. When `folder = ''` the arg keeps a **trailing slash**: `/tmp/probe-5/vaultloc/v1/`; in subfolder `sub`: `/tmp/probe-5/vaultloc/v1/sub` (no trailing slash); with `folder = 'nope'`: `/tmp/probe-5/vaultloc/v1/nope` (nonexistent path still passed verbatim).
- **Does not wait** for `xdg-open` (returned in ~3 ms while the stub slept 2 s; only the stub's pre-sleep log line existed at return). Child exit code ignored (stub `exit 3` → jt 0). Child **inherits stdout/stderr** (stub's `XDG-STDOUT`/`XDG-STDERR` appeared on jt's streams).
- On success jt prints nothing, exit 0.
- `xdg-open` not on PATH: stdout `\x1b[0;31merror\x1b[0m: undefined error: No such file or directory (os error 2)\n`, exit 0. (Note: unlike `open`, this is *not* the "editor not found" message.)
- `xdg-open` present but not executable: stdout `\x1b[0;31merror\x1b[0m: undefined error: Permission denied (os error 13)\n`, exit 0.
- Does not consult the `editor` config at all.
- Corrupted `.jot/data` → panic exit 101 (`src/traits.rs:24:21: couldn't parse data`). Missing vault dir → same skeleton-file recreation as `open`, then panic exit 101 at `src/state/vaults/vault.rs:55:32` (open panics at line 44, opdir at 55 — column `:28` vs `:32`).
- No state-file side effects on success.

---

## 4. Reimplementation cheat-sheet

- Blue = `\x1b[0;34m...\x1b[0m`, red error prefix = `\x1b[0;31merror\x1b[0m: `; all app messages end with `\n` and go to **stdout** with exit 0.
- `config <key>` → `<key>: <blue(value)>`; `config <key> <val>` → `set <blue(key)> to <blue(val)>`; keys restricted to `editor|conflict` by the CLI parser itself; `conflict` values other than `true`/`false` panic (exit 101).
- Editor invocation (`config` bare, `open`): exec `config.editor` literally (no splitting), one argv = target file, wait, ignore exit status, inherit stdio; missing → `error: editor not found`; spawn errors → `error: undefined error: <os error>`.
- `open`: "not inside a vault" → name validation (`/` or `\` → "invalid name") → resolve `<folder>/<file_stem(name)>.md` (with `..` → path as-is, `.` → never found) → `exists()` → spawn editor, else `error: note <name> not found`.
- `opdir`: spawn `xdg-open "<location>/<name>/<folder>"` (string concat; trailing slash when folder is empty), detached, inherit stdio, print nothing.
